clue.text: In which government plans men to be gathered by actor Tree, after polling

indicators.note: the men are taken in, gathered up inside the word for the actor

parts.note: THESP is a short informal word for a thespian, an actor
in chess the pieces are called men, and queens are among them

indicators.note: polling a tree is lopping its top, so the first letter of the tree's name is removed

parts.note: the beech is a tree; Herbert Beerbohm Tree was also a famous actor

explanation.surface: A tale of theatrical recruiting by the Victorian actor-manager Tree once the votes are in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'actor Tree' reads as Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager, but the two words work separately. Chessmen include queens, and polling a tree means pollarding, cutting off its top.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's address opening Parliament sets out the legislative programme the government intends.

clue.text: Cruise, or line that never arrives

parts.note: Tom Cruise, the film actor
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A Tom Cruise film or a line of cars that never turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial day after today is always one day off, so it never actually comes.

clue.text: I was in the van, going up to the shop

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to be in the van (vanguard) is to be at the front, to have led

explanation.surface: Someone recalls riding in a delivery van up to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' suggests a vehicle, but 'in the van' means at the front, so LED.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: "Victory" — focus of flagship vessel to find a measure of knots, say?

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: the focus of a word is its centre, so the middle pair of letters is taken

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: Nelson's flagship Victory and a measure of a ship's speed in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Victory' and 'flagship' the knots seem nautical, but knots are wading birds, so the measure is their span from wingtip to wingtip.
explanation.definitionFit: Wingspan measures the width of a bird such as the knot, a sandpiper, with wings spread.

clue.text: Shocked at inhaling hydrogen in its normal state

indicators.note: inhaling takes something inside, so the word at surrounds the rest
the hydrogen symbol is placed in the word for its state

parts.note: hydrogen is normally a gas
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to be breathing in hydrogen gas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aghast is to be filled with horror or shock.

clue.text: Copper stealing kiss was mistaken for crew member

indicators.note: the coin takes the other letters into itself, as though pocketing them

parts.note: a copper is a low-value coin
X is the conventional symbol for a kiss

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters of the word was are put wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman snatching a kiss is mistaken for one of the boat's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman or Cu; it is a coin. 'mistaken' turns WAS into SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxswain is the crew member who steers a boat.

clue.text: Runner needing momentum to bag runs

indicators.note: to bag is to put in a bag, so the runs letter goes inside

parts.note: steam is momentum, as in gaining or losing steam
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sprinter needs momentum to rack up runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but water runs, so a stream is a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is something that runs, flowing water, so it is fairly called a runner.

clue.text: Our feature on which questions end and are dealt with?

definitions.text: Our feature on which questions end and are dealt with?

parts.words: Our feature on which questions end and are dealt with?
parts.note: the newspaper's own long-running column where readers post questions and other readers answer them

explanation.surface: The paper boasts of a column where readers' questions get answered.
explanation.definitionFit: This Guardian feature printed readers' queries and other readers' replies to them.

clue.text: Domestic chore completed in accessing corner

indicators.note: the two pieces get into the word for corner, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to corner something, as in a market, is to hog it
something completed is over

explanation.surface: A household job is done in reaching an awkward corner.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOVERING is British for vacuum cleaning, after the Hoover brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Running the vacuum cleaner is a routine piece of housework.

clue.text: Better party alfresco?

parts.note: alfresco means outdoors, out
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Is an open-air party an improvement?
explanation.definitionFit: To better someone is to surpass or outdo them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: One in five claims books good for copying out text

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so the books go inside

parts.note: a quin is one of five children born together, a quintuplet
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A quintuplet claims a book was good for transcription.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting is reproducing someone else's words exactly, copying a passage.

clue.text: Cold sea true to form

indicators.note: the letters of sea true are made into a new form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A chilly sea behaves just as you'd expect.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere manners are stern and unfriendly, which is a cold way of behaving.

clue.text: English vineyard providing light shade

parts.note: a cru is a French wine-growing estate or its classified wine

explanation.surface: An English vineyard gives some welcome shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow colour, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Seeing limitation work, one brought into game after half-time

indicators.note: after puts the game, with its insert, behind the half-time letters

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the one is brought into the game, inside its letters

parts.note: halma is a board game of moving pieces across a grid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone with poor sight is brought on as a substitute after half-time.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflammation of the eye limits the sufferer's vision.

clue.text: Past follows present? Let me see

indicators.note: follows puts the past word after the present one

parts.note: the present moment is now
then refers to a past time

explanation.surface: A puzzled musing on time: does the past come after the present?
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic fillers said while pausing to think something over.

clue.text: Unpleasant person in gardener, perhaps, in trouble when in this?

indicators.note: the unpleasant person is put in the gardener's word

parts.note: a hoer, someone using a hoe, is one sort of gardener
twat is a vulgar British term for an obnoxious person

explanation.surface: A nasty person in the garden is going to be in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in hot water is an idiom for being in trouble.

clue.text: Cool before dice shaken, as expected to win

parts.note: to fan something is to cool it

indicators.note: dice that are shaken land jumbled, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler stays calm before rolling, fancying a win.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancied runner is one tipped or expected to come first.

clue.text: Trees harbouring the kernel of arcane prophecy

indicators.note: harbouring means holding inside, so the trees' word surrounds the kernel

parts.note: a forest is a large area of trees

indicators.note: a kernel is a core, so the central letters are taken

explanation.surface: A wood conceals the heart of an ancient mystic prophecy.
explanation.definitionFit: A forecast is a prediction of what is to come, a kind of prophecy.

clue.text: Major bid may be a lot

definitions.meaning: a bid in a major suit at bridge
an idiom meaning in great quantity or abundantly

explanation.definitionFit: Spades is a major suit in bridge, and the phrase also idiomatically means plenty.

clue.text: Fabl?

parts.note: a word for a tale is printed lacking its final letter, so it is literally a tale cut short

explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a tale, and this one is shortened by a letter.

clue.text: Oliver Twist, perhaps, in many instances in 1 down

indicators.note: the royal accent of 1 down's speaker is the pronunciation used

parts.note: something happening in many instances happens often

explanation.surface: Dickens's Oliver crops up again and again in the monarch's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 1 down' means as spoken in the Queen's cut-glass accent, where often comes out sounding like orfen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Oliver Twist is a child whose parents are dead, an example of the type.

clue.text: Game, or six of them, holding local up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole assembly is read backwards
holding means the set surrounds the pub word

parts.note: six games win a set in this very sport
a local is a neighbourhood pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A game, or a set of six, held up at the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SINNET (INN held in SET). 'local' is British for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, a game played in sets.

clue.text: Hairy man occupying the sauna

indicators.note: occupying means sitting within, so the name is found inside the words

explanation.surface: A hirsute man is sitting in the sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau, Jacob's brother, is described as a hairy man.

clue.text: Clarify, so now complicated?

definitions.meaning: to make something clear or understandable
read whimsically as formerly plain, no longer simple, hence now complicated

explanation.definitionFit: To clarify is to make a matter clear, and split it reads as a former plain thing.

clue.text: Pirate's audibly rough manner

indicators.note: audibly means the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a coarse air is a rough manner

explanation.surface: A buccaneer has a coarse way about him.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, originally one sailing the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Skin that's hard as a ball in 1 down

indicators.note: the royal accent of 1 down's speaker is the pronunciation used

parts.note: a ball is round

explanation.surface: A tough skin is likened to a ball in a royal address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 1 down' means in the Queen's clipped accent, where round is heard as rind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin of fruit or cheese.

clue.text: Box for old wheels

definitions.meaning: slang for a decrepit old car, wheels being slang for a vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a packing case, and also slang for a battered old car.

clue.text: Where cohabitants live, the Church about to prove false

parts.note: unmarried couples living together were once said to be living in sin
CE is the Church of England
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Unmarried couples and the Church about to be shown up as hypocrites.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insincere is false, not meaning what they say.
